title: Relationships in SQL
definition: Relationships define how tables are connected to each other using primary keys and foreign keys.

one_to_one.heading: One-to-One Relationship
one_to_one.definition: One record in table A is related to exactly one record in table B.
one_to_one.query: CREATE TABLE users (user_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, username VARCHAR(100));

one_to_many.heading: One-to-Many Relationship
one_to_many.definition: One record in table A can be related to multiple records in table B.

customers.query: CREATE TABLE customers (cust_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, cust_name VARCHAR(100));

orders.query: CREATE TABLE orders (order_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, order_date DATE, price NUMERIC, cust_id INT, FOREIGN KEY (cust_id) REFERENCES customers(cust_id));

many_to_many.heading: Many-to-Many Relationship
many_to_many.definition: Many records in table A can relate to many records in table B using a junction table.

students.query: CREATE TABLE students (student_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100));

courses.query: CREATE TABLE courses (course_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, course_name VARCHAR(100));

enrollment.query: CREATE TABLE enrollment (enroll_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, student_id INT, course_id INT, FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES students(student_id), FOREIGN KEY (course_id) REFERENCES courses(course_id));
